summary: All four reviews converge on the designed defect and its bounded remedy: legacy labels are computed at module load under the import-time 'en' locale while the two new entries use read-time getters, so after setLocale('ru') the six-option group returns mixed languages through listCategoryOptions and labelForCategory, and saveSelection snapshots the wrong creation-time text for legacy IDs. Each review notes base pre-existence but keeps the defect in scope because the brief preserves the README contract, and each proposes completing current-locale behavior for the shared group (getters, factory, or t at call time) without breaking IDs/order or the historical snapshot — matching the rubric's F1 hit. Each also matches the F2 hit: the suite switches locale only for the new entries, so stale legacy labels pass; the proposed remedy is a post-import locale switch checking old and new labels through both public reads. No review triggers X1 (all extend lazy reads rather than undoing them), X2 (all keep the copy-on-save lifetime, u04 most explicitly), or X3 (all treat the contract as data-only and static). Mechanism identification and behavior preservation are supported for all; necessityAndCost is supported for all because each makes an explicit reuse-based decision rather than merely listing costs; responsibilityBoundaries is not_applicable for all, since the fixture demonstrates no structural problem and the reviews' keep statements are bounded. The four reports form one equivalence group; the case's discriminating power here lay in trap avoidance and dimension discipline, where all four also align.
